Quote source · Q0259

Who said “What is rational is actual; and what is actual is rational”?

The located source for this passage, the original-language wording where one exists, and the forms of it that circulate without the attribution.

Quote source / G. W. F. Hegel / What is rational is actual;…

English

What is rational is actual; and what is actual is rational.
Thinker G. W. F. Hegel
Work Philosophy of Right, Preface
School German Idealism
Theme Reason

Checked against the cited edition on 2026-09-27.

The recorded source

Attributed to
G. W. F. Hegel
Work and locator
Philosophy of Right, Preface
English wording
“What is rational is actual; and what is actual is rational.”
Original wording (German)
Was vernünftig ist, das ist wirklich; und was wirklich ist, das ist vernünftig.

Preface to the Philosophy of Right. English “actual” for wirklich is the standard philosophical choice; “real” invites a cruder reading Hegel spent the preface blocking.

Exact wording and the variants in circulation

A quotation in English from a non-English source has two versions, and they are not interchangeable.

The wording recorded here is the one this archive holds. These are the forms that circulate in its place:

  • “What is rational is actual; and what is actual is rational.”
  • “The real is rational and the rational is real.”

Attribution notes

Hegel, Elements of the Philosophy of Right, Preface (1820). The sloganized “the real is rational” is the version critics attacked; Hegel's wirklich is “actual” in the sense of what has developed into its concept, not “whatever happens to exist.” Quoting the English without that distinction is how the line became a caricature of apologetics.
